title: Rav Pappa bar Abba Rishba
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: [Chullin 54a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.54a) relates that they struck (the animal) on the kidney and killed it, and came before Rabbi Abba. Yuchasin did not list him. Seder HaDorot explains that he was not a sage, and conjectures that the reading should be “the household of Pappa bar Abba.” This explains the precise wording “they came before him,” rather than “he came.” A sage is superior to a prophet: this is indeed the reading in the Soncino printing, as cited in Dikdukei Soferim.[^1]

notes.text: לא הביאו concerns not listing the person, rather than not citing an incident. The ordinary work abbreviations סה״ד and דק״ס are rendered Seder HaDorot and Dikdukei Soferim; “Sefer HaDorot” in the earlier English is corrected. Hyman’s printed alternative is דבי פפא בר אבא, “the household of Pappa bar Abba.” His argument contrasts plural אתו with singular אתא; “a sage is superior to a prophet” praises the conjecture’s confirmation by the Soncino reading. The attribution of the conjecture to Seder HaDorot follows the immediate grammar; no independent quotation boundary or edition has been established. The animal parenthesis is Hyman’s, and the printed heading רישבא is not replaced with the catalog alias דישבא. Chullin נד. is conventionally 54a; neither that passage nor the Soncino claim was checked here.
